plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE with effect-size triage
plan.analytical_narrative: 60 cases vs 60 controls, single batch, unpaired, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 121 samples incl. metadata rows) is a population-scale cohort. At n=60/arm, sample-to-sample biological variance in a real cohort does not follow the negative binomial assumption of DESeq2/edgeR, and count models have been shown to produce excess false positives even on permuted labels at this scale (Mishra et al., Genome Biology 2022 / R-0015). The knowledge base therefore grounds the primary test as limma-voom with TMM normalization, with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test run as a permutation-style robustness control. The research question explicitly separates statistical significance from magnitude ('large enough to matter, not only significant'), so the plan (a) runs QC first to confirm the cohort has no batch/outlier structure hidden under 'single batch', (b) filters and normalizes minimally so the FDR/independent-filtering machinery keeps its power, (c) tests for a fold-change threshold directly (TREAT/glmTreat) rather than post-hoc filtering a p-value list by fold change, which has no error-rate control, (d) reports shrunken effect sizes (apeglm) alongside the raw estimates and ranks the significant gene table by effect size, and (e) runs enrichment (camera + fgsea preranked on moderated t) against Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways to characterize which coordinated programs move, using the tested-gene universe throughout. Every step is grounded against the Inflexa full_plan/enrichment procedures for this exact situation (n=60/60, unpaired, single batch, salmon counts, human) and the enrichment step passed the automated knowledge_check with no violations.
